dicas.texto: Look at the numerator and denominator of each fraction and think about what part of one whole each student read.
A fraction less than 1 has a numerator smaller than its denominator.
Both numerators are 1, while the denominators are 4 and 5.
Select the fraction that represents Levar's amount, using 1 as the numerator and 4 as the denominator.
Which number in a fraction tells how many equal parts form the whole?
Read the denominator, the bottom number, and enter that number in the field.
In 1/4, the bottom number is 4.
Type the denominator from 1/4 into the denom1 field and confirm the division.
Think about how far one of the four equal parts is from 0.
Start at 0 and count the number of intervals named by the numerator.
The numerator is 1, so mark the first division after 0.
Click the first tick after 0 on the line divided into four equal intervals.
Each fraction can have its own number of equal parts. Which number controls Laura's division?
Read the bottom number in Laura's fraction and enter it in the denominator field.
The denominator in 1/5 is 5.
Type 5 in the denom2 field and confirm to create five equal intervals.
Use the number line to show how much of the whole Laura has read.
Begin at 0 and count one interval because the numerator is 1.
Laura's line has five equal intervals, so the first tick after 0 represents one fifth.
Click the first tick after 0 on the line divided into five equal intervals.
Compare the sizes of the fractions, not only the numbers written underneath.
Look at the distance of each marked point from 0 on its correctly divided line.
With one selected part, dividing the whole into more parts makes each part smaller.
Identify the fraction represented by the comparison target and select the value shown for Levar's amount.
Match the selected statement to the student and fraction identified in the comparison.
Read each option carefully and compare its student name with the marked fraction.
Choose the option that names Levar as the student who read less.
In the compBox selector, choose the statement beginning with Levar and ending with "less of the novel."
Before submitting, review the fraction represented by the selected comparison.
Check that both number lines were divided and that both points were marked.
Verify that the selected comparison is still visible in the compBox selector.
After checking the selected statement and the fraction value, press the Done button.

exercicio.statement:
Levar and Laura are reading a novel as a class assignment. Use the number line to find out which student has read less of the novel.
Levar has read 1/4 of the novel.
Laura has read 1/5 of the novel.
Who has read less of the novel?
